# Throwing away local edits: revert takes the server's version, keeping a
# copy of what was discarded — the one destructive verb, made recoverable.

fulcrum sync
cp mine.md skills/skill-corpus-writing-specs.md
fulcrum -code 1 status
grep 'drifted' last-stdout.txt

# Declining changes nothing.
fulcrum -in decline.txt revert skill-corpus-writing-specs
grep 'Nothing to revert' last-stdout.txt
cmp skills/skill-corpus-writing-specs.md mine.md

# Confirming restores the server's bytes and keeps mine aside.
fulcrum -in accept.txt revert skill-corpus-writing-specs
grep 'reverted skill-corpus-writing-specs.md' last-stdout.txt
grep 'your version is kept at' last-stdout.txt
cmp skills/skill-corpus-writing-specs.md $CORPUS/documents/skill-corpus-writing-specs.md
cmp skills/.fulcrum/discarded/skill-corpus-writing-specs.md mine.md
fulcrum status
! grep 'drifted' last-stdout.txt

# It also rescues a deleted file, and --yes skips the prompt.
rm skills/skill-corpus-writing-specs.md
fulcrum -code 1 status
grep 'missing' last-stdout.txt
fulcrum revert skill-corpus-writing-specs --yes
cmp skills/skill-corpus-writing-specs.md $CORPUS/documents/skill-corpus-writing-specs.md

# A name that is not a document says so rather than silently doing nothing.
fulcrum -code 2 revert not-a-document --yes
grep 'no document named' last-stderr.txt

-- mine.md --
---
name: corpus-writing-specs
description: How this team writes request specs.
---

# corpus-writing-specs

Mine, and I have changed my mind about it.
-- decline.txt --
n
-- accept.txt --
y
